title: STEM gifts for kids UK 2026: science kits, coding robots and boxes
description: The best STEM gifts for kids this Christmas, from a £6 slime lab to coding robots and Lego Technic, by age, with UK prices checked on 2 November.
intro:
**Our top STEM gift for most kids this Christmas is the Learning Resources Cooper coding robot at £60 from Argos, £10 less than elsewhere, and it needs no screen.** On a smaller budget, the Science Museum scorpion robot kit is £20 at The Entertainer, and Argos has Galt's slime lab at £6, its lowest price yet.

Every price below was checked on 2 November 2026. We've grouped ideas by age, said what's worth buying now, and covered science subscription boxes like Tinkerer for a gift that keeps arriving.

body:
## How to choose a STEM gift

STEM stands for science, technology, engineering and maths. The best STEM gifts don't feel like homework. They're toys a child wants to play with, and the learning happens along the way. A few things to check before you buy:

- **Match the age, then go slightly up.** Age labels on science kits are about safety and reading level. A confident 7-year-old will often enjoy an 8+ kit with a little help, but a kit aimed far above their age usually ends up abandoned.
- **One big moment beats twenty small ones.** Kits with a clear result, like a robot that moves or a geode that cracks open, get finished. Huge chemistry sets with dozens of small experiments often don't.
- **Screens are optional.** Robots like Cooper and Botley teach the basics of coding with buttons, which suits younger children and parents who'd rather avoid another app.
- **Check the batteries.** Robots and circuit kits rarely include them. Add a pack of AA or AAA to your order.

## Best STEM gifts by age

**Ages 3–5:** keep it simple and hands-on. Botley 2.0 (£70) is the classic first coding robot. For a smaller gift, a magnetic building set or a big magnifying glass does more than a complicated kit.

**Ages 5–8:** this is the sweet spot for coding robots and messy science. Cooper (£60 at Argos) or the £6 slime lab, depending on your budget. A [Lego set from our Lego Black Friday guide](/guides/lego-black-friday-deals-2026/) also counts: building to instructions is real engineering practice.

**Ages 8–12:** robot construction kits like the £20 scorpion, rocks-and-minerals kits and Lego Technic. The Artemis rocket (£55) is a good bridge between Lego and real space science.

**Teens:** a Raspberry Pi 400 kit (£76.80) turns into whatever they want it to be: a games emulator, a coding project or a home server. The Lego Technic Ford GT40 (£65 at The Entertainer, age 18+) suits an older teen who likes cars, though stock is low.

## Science subscription boxes

A subscription box makes a good gift from grandparents, because it keeps arriving after Christmas. **Tinkerer** (tinkererbox.com) is a UK STEAM box with three age ranges: Wonder (3–5), Odyssey (6–8) and Explore (9–12). Each monthly box holds 3–5 projects around a theme, such as building a working stethoscope while learning about the body. Tinkerer's prices weren't visible when we checked, so compare its current monthly and prepaid options on the site before you buy. A fixed-length prepaid gift is usually easier than an open-ended monthly plan.

## What's a good price?

Coding robots for young children usually cost £50–£80, so £60 for Cooper is fair. Robot construction kits from known brands sit around £20–£40, and good science kits around £20–£35. Be wary of very cheap unbranded kits on marketplaces: parts are often missing and instructions poor.

## When do prices drop?

Black Friday is on **Friday 27 November 2026**. Lego and big-brand robots are the most likely to be cut then; see [when is Black Friday 2026](/guides/when-is-black-friday-2026-uk/) for every retailer's dates. But several picks here are already on low stock, and popular Lego Technic sets tend to sell out before December. If a set is on your list and the price is fair, don't gamble on it. For more ideas, see all our [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/), including [Secret Santa gifts under £10](/guides/secret-santa-gifts-under-10/).

### What is a good STEM gift for a 6-year-old?

A screen-free coding robot like Learning Resources Cooper (£60) or a simple messy science kit. Both give a quick, visible result, which is what keeps a 6-year-old interested.

### Are STEM subscription boxes worth it?

Yes, if the child likes making things. A box arriving each month keeps the excitement going after Christmas. Where you can, choose a prepaid gift option rather than an open-ended monthly one, so nobody has to remember to cancel.

### Will STEM toys be cheaper on Black Friday?

Lego and well-known brands are the most likely to be cut. Smaller science kits tend to change less. If stock is already low, as with several Lego Technic sets, buy now at a fair price.

### What STEM gift suits a teenager?

A Raspberry Pi kit is hard to beat, as it's a real computer they can program and build with. An adult Lego Technic set suits teens who prefer building to coding.
